title: Make your codepix folder
prompt:
Today you only need Terminal. Open it from Spotlight by typing Terminal, or from the Utilities folder inside Applications [py-001]. Then type these, pressing Return after each one: `pwd`, `mkdir codepix`, `cd codepix`, `pwd`, `ls`.

The second `pwd` should end in `codepix`, and `ls` prints nothing yet, because the folder is empty.

The file `where.py` is Byte's tiny program. Python is not on your machine until A1, so save it in the folder now and run it after A1. It prints the same thing `pwd` does.
hints: Type each command exactly, then press Return. Spaces matter: `mkdir codepix` has one space in it.
If `mkdir` says the folder already exists, that is fine. Skip to `cd codepix`.
Lost? `pwd` always tells you where you are, and `cd ..` takes you up one folder.
explain_after: `pwd` printed your working directory, `cd` changed it, and `ls` listed what is inside [py-003]. `mkdir` made the new folder [py-007]. After A1, `python3 where.py` prints the same path that `pwd` printed, and the test checks that it does.
